town.name: Brightwater · Festival District
town.description: Festival roads cross gardens, homes, fields, and the river while two processions wait for the truth.

objects.name: Festival banner
objects.text: A rising sun and two stitched oaks flank the eastern gate. The cloth is dated 1907.

objects.name: Monument foundation
objects.text: The old socket points east. Fresh tool scratches curve around the newer north-facing arrow.

objects.name: Aster Finch
objects.text: I stopped rehearsal when the two processions split. The old banner points east, but the official atlas sends everyone north. Start with Mira Vale in the coral-roofed cartography house beyond the eastern gardens, then compare what she shows you with the banner here in the rehearsal meadow.

objects.name: Rest & refill vitality
objects.text: You rest, refill your sun pips, and record your progress.

cartography.name: Vale Cartography
cartography.description: Mira keeps the sources close, and her conclusions in pencil.

objects.name: The annotated atlas
objects.text: Northern road. Margin: Route updated from temporary survey copy. The map was published in 1912.

objects.name: Mira Vale
objects.text: Lay that old east-pointing banner beside this official northern map, marked 'temporary survey copy,' Liora. Compare their lines carefully and tell me what differences you find. The two processions each carry a piece of the story. Read the atlas margin, then compare the banner and the monument. An official map can faithfully copy a temporary source.

objects.name: Rest & refill vitality
objects.text: You rest, refill your sun pips, and record your progress.

hall.name: Brightwater Council Hall & Civic Archive
hall.description: A public record can preserve a mistake as carefully as a truth.

objects.name: Councilor Varn
objects.text: The council is meeting because neither procession will yield. I maintain the northern road, and I will not send a festival crowd across a broken ford merely because an older banner points east. Bring me evidence for a route that respects history and keeps people safe.

objects.name: Sign painter’s receipt
objects.text: Remove temporary from the northern road signs; repaint the destination as warehouse road.

objects.name: Festival programs
objects.text: 1908: emergency detour. 1912: northern route. 1916: traditional northern road. Repetition slowly replaced qualification.

objects.name: Varn maintenance charter
objects.text: The Varn family inherited upkeep of the northern road after its adoption. The charter does not establish involvement in the 1908 decision.

forest.name: Sunleaf · Twin Oaks
forest.description: Fresh paint shines on an old trail. The bark remembers another line.

objects.name: Eastern boundary stones
objects.text: Three worn sun symbols line up between Brightwater and the twin oaks. Their cuts sit beneath recent paint.

objects.name: Twin oak notches
objects.text: Beneath the paint, paired old cuts face the eastern boundary stones. The trees and song preserve the same line.

objects.name: Rest & refill vitality

lodge.name: Ranger Lodge
lodge.description: Orin has been listening to this forest longer than most maps have existed.

objects.name: Procession song
objects.text: Through the twin crowns, toward the dawn; past the river, to the public shore. The verse is preserved on an old shelter board.

objects.name: Orin Moss
objects.text: Recent paint is easy to see; old cuts take patience. The lodge song, boundary stones, and bark should be compared. Take this Wayfinder staff. Use Space to clear loose branches and gently turn away creatures.

objects.name: Rest & refill vitality

river.name: Silverrun · Reedbank
river.description: Water changed the road. It did not erase the reasons.

objects.name: Ferryman’s log
objects.text: 1908: The river rose beyond the chapel mark. The stone ford broke. Travelers were sent north until repairs could make a crossing safe.

objects.name: Northern bridge receipt
objects.text: Emergency northern access: timber and labor purchased after the 1908 flood.

objects.name: Broken ford survey
objects.text: The ford stones remain undermined. Even at low water, a crowded procession would be unsafe.

objects.name: Tavi Reed
objects.text: That ford is still broken. Read the log and receipt before judging the detour. In the sluice house, leave one channel for the reeds and two for the ferry. Take my river line.

sluice.description: Three channels share one river: the mill, the ferry, and the nesting reeds.

objects.name: Sela Marr
objects.text: This lens shows repairs beneath the glaze. In the Hall of Copies, turn each map toward its source: first survey, then tablet, then atlas. Leave unsupported parts blank.

objects.name: Inez Sol
objects.text: The lighthouse can show you the islands. The lens carriage remembers a short, long, short signal. Take a signal lantern. Public access is a promise we must keep safely.

objects.name: Cira’s orchard journal
objects.text: The eastern orchard survived because neighbors kept sharing grafts and water after the public route moved. A quiet act of memory. Your festival gains orchard lanterns.

objects.name: The distant Wayfinder light

objects.name: Wayfinder storm shelter
objects.text: A wind mantle rests beside the shelter record. Hold Shift to steady your pace; the mantle protects against wind. Marked circles warn of falling stone.

objects.name: Help the stranded council
objects.text: You secure the river line across the damaged steps. The council members cross one at a time. The safe ascent is open.

summit.description: The whole valley lies below. Now make the case for its future.

objects.name: Light the living line
objects.text: The council approves the living route. Varn accepts its safety plan. From Brightwater to the public shore, torches join into one bright line. Your compass rests, then pulses once toward the distant islands.

banner.title: Festival banner
banner.text: A rising sun and two stitched oaks flank the eastern gate. The cloth is dated 1907.
banner.limitation: A ceremonial image suggests landmarks, but is not a survey.

atlas.title: The annotated atlas
atlas.text: Northern road. Margin: Route updated from temporary survey copy. The map was published in 1912.
atlas.limitation: The map is official, but its source was temporary.

foundation.title: Monument foundation
foundation.text: The old socket points east. Fresh tool scratches curve around the newer north-facing arrow.
foundation.limitation: Wear establishes alteration, not the date or motive.

stones.title: Eastern boundary stones
stones.text: Three worn sun symbols line up between Brightwater and the twin oaks. Their cuts sit beneath recent paint.
stones.limitation: The stones support an alignment, not its present safety.

song.title: Procession song
song.text: Through the twin crowns, toward the dawn; past the river, to the public shore. The verse is preserved on an old shelter board.
song.limitation: Songs can change in transmission; compare the land.

notches.title: Twin oak notches
notches.text: Beneath the paint, paired old cuts face the eastern boundary stones. The trees and song preserve the same line.
notches.limitation: Tree marks do not explain why the road was abandoned.

log.title: Ferryman’s log
log.text: 1908: The river rose beyond the chapel mark. The stone ford broke. Travelers were sent north until repairs could make a crossing safe.
log.limitation: A firsthand record of the flood, not the later mapmaking.

receipt.title: Northern bridge receipt
receipt.text: Emergency northern access: timber and labor purchased after the 1908 flood.
receipt.limitation: A payment establishes work, not permanent route status.

survey.title: Broken ford survey
survey.text: The ford stones remain undermined. Even at low water, a crowded procession would be unsafe.
survey.limitation: Conditions may change; this inspection applies now.

tablet.title: Replacement tablet
tablet.text: New glaze surrounds the northern detour. A chipped double notch occurs in both this 1909 replacement and the later atlas.
tablet.limitation: Durable material does not make a copied route original.

ledger.title: Repair ledger
ledger.text: 1909: Transfer the temporary survey line to the replacement tablet pending review. One later page has been torn out.
ledger.limitation: The missing page limits what this volume can prove.

tracing.title: Atlas tracing sheet
tracing.text: A tracing overlays the tablet’s northern line and reproduces its double notch. It bears the atlas workshop seal.
tracing.limitation: This connects copying, but does not identify a later motive.

handbill.title: Merchant handbill
handbill.text: 1913: The OFFICIAL festival road ends at the northern warehouses. Supplies, storage, and lodging available.
handbill.limitation: Advertising reveals an interest; it does not alone prove manipulation.

missing.title: The missing ledger page
missing.text: The consortium asks clerks to retain the warehouse destination and omit temporary from the route description. The torn edge matches the repair ledger.
missing.limitation: It proves this request, not that every civic worker agreed.

accounts.title: Warehouse account book
accounts.text: Festival storage and lodging income rose after travelers were directed to the warehouses.
accounts.limitation: Income supports benefit, but benefit alone does not prove intent.

signs.title: Sign painter’s receipt
signs.text: Remove temporary from the northern road signs; repaint the destination as warehouse road.
signs.limitation: Records an instruction; does not explain every resident’s belief.

programs.title: Festival programs
programs.text: 1908: emergency detour. 1912: northern route. 1916: traditional northern road. Repetition slowly replaced qualification.
programs.limitation: Programs show public language, not private motives.

charter.title: Varn maintenance charter
charter.text: The Varn family inherited upkeep of the northern road after its adoption. The charter does not establish involvement in the 1908 decision.
charter.limitation: Inherited responsibility is not proof of originating the deception.

accord.title: Coastkeeper Accord
accord.text: The three island fragments share a seal: Beacon Point is held for public access.
accord.limitation: Public rights still require a safe physical access route.

ferrytest.title: Modern ferry safety test
ferrytest.text: A restored drive, balanced cargo, and protected reed channel passed a supervised crossing.
ferrytest.limitation: The crossing needs ongoing maintenance and weather checks.

habitat.title: Habitat survey
habitat.text: The old forest line can reopen if traffic stays on marked ground and nesting reeds retain flow.
habitat.limitation: Seasonal changes will require later review.

access.title: Public access inspection
access.text: A marked coastal walkway reaches the lawful shore above the sensitive tide pools.
access.limitation: Access must close during dangerous storms.

opening.name: Turn the plaza arrow
opening.text: The foundation socket is older than the rotated arrow. Align the arrow with the old socket; compare the two procession sources first.

forest.name: Align the boundary markers
forest.text: Orin’s shelter verse names the route in order: twin crowns, river, public shore. Rotate the three markers to carry that sequence through the grove.

sluice.name: Balance the sluice
sluice.text: The brass plate reads: four units total. One for the mill, two for the ferry, one for nesting reeds. Closing the reeds would drain a habitat. Set each gate.

river.name: Rebuild the flood sequence
river.text: Fit the events into Tavi’s timeline rack. Use the dated log and receipt: water rises, the ford breaks, then northern access opens.

copies.name: Turn the source gallery
copies.text: Turn each gallery frame toward the source it copied. The ledger names the temporary survey as the tablet’s source. The tracing carries the tablet’s flaw into the atlas.

guardian.name: Reset the route guardian
guardian.text: The guardian pulses across the chamber. Its maintenance panel asks for the original route stations: oaks, river, shore. Rebuild its sequence to make the chamber safe.

beacon.name: Restore the beacon signal
beacon.text: Inez taught the harbor call: short, long, short. Set the three shutters. The charted island passages will open.

coast.name: Assemble the public shore case
coast.text: Inez’s case table has places for ownership, action, and benefit. Fit the records according to what each can actually show.

civic.name: Ring the civic timeline
civic.text: Ring the four dated plates in sequence. The records trace change through emergency, copying, promotion, then removal of qualifying language. Varn inherited road maintenance; these records do not make him the original author.

ferry.name: Test the public ferry
ferry.text: A safe crossing needs a balanced deck, a secured river line, and steady flow. Tavi’s test plate: passengers left, counterweight right, river line secured.

habitat_route.name: Protect the grove route
habitat_route.text: Orin points out nesting ground beside the old marks. Keep people on the marked trail, maintain a rope edge, and leave nests undisturbed.

markers.name: Authenticate the route markers
markers.text: Sela’s lens separates old edges from guesswork. Restore the supported east alignment; keep the missing section visibly blank.

access_route.name: Open the shore walkway
access_route.text: Inez proposes an elevated marked walkway. It protects the pools and keeps access public, with storm closures.

route.name: Build the living route
route.text: Mira’s route board must honor the evidence and today’s conditions. The ford is unsafe. Keep the eastern line, use the tested ferry, pass the authenticated ruins, and reach public shore.

synthesis.name: Present the living route
synthesis.text: Varn asks: how does this proposal answer the ford? Present the tested ferry, distinguish benefit from proof of pressure, and acknowledge maintenance. The council needs a qualified case, not certainty without evidence.

echoes.name: Answer the island bells
echoes.text: The carved bell score reads low, high, middle. Each bell also flashes its name so the pattern can be read without sound.

underpath.name: Wake the old conduits
underpath.text: The maintenance diagram combines the river and beacon rules: reeds one, ferry two, lantern long. Carry those working settings into the old system.

worksheets: Before leaving Brightwater, predict which direction the historic Sunpath followed. Use one detail from the banner and one from the atlas or monument.
Which two discoveries most strongly support the eastern forest route? Explain how they reinforce each other.
Why did Brightwater change the route after 1908? Was the original decision reasonable? Support both parts.
Explain how the temporary detour became part of the official atlas. Identify one source limitation.
Who benefited from the northern route, and what evidence shows that benefit? Explain why motive alone does not prove the case.
Recommend the modern festival route. Use at least four sources from three regions, address the broken ford, and explain one limitation or tradeoff.
